A potential strike at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach has been pushed back to midnight Pacific time Friday night, Nov. 6, after employers and the union representing about 250 port watchmen agreed to extend their contract. The extension gives negotiators more time to reach a deal at the country’s busiest container port complex.
What’s Related
The Pacific Maritime Association, which represents terminal employers and ocean carriers, announced the extension as talks with International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 continue. It replaces a previous deadline of 5 p.m. Pacific time Wednesday, Nov. 4.
“Negotiations will continue on Friday with the help of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service,” PMA said in its statement. The agreement extends the existing contract while bargaining continues; PMA has not announced a replacement contract.
Local 26 represents watchmen who perform security duties at marine terminals. PMA estimates that the affected terminals handle more than half of the two ports’ combined cargo , including roughly 85% at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles.
RELATED: Top 30 U.S. Ports Ranked By Container Imports In 2025
More than just security
The PMA says watchmen make up about 2% of the ILWU workforce at the two ports. But the employer group has warned that a walkout could also interrupt work performed by other union members.
Dockworkers and marine clerks have separate labor contracts and are not part of the watchmen’s negotiations. PMA said it expects those workers to honor Local 26 picket lines, potentially stopping ship loading and unloading, container movements in terminal yards, and truck access at affected terminals.
Those consequences remain conditional on a strike and other workers’ response. The cargo percentages reflect terminals employers say could be disrupted , not cargo already delayed by a walkout.
More Than a Year of Bargaining
The watchmen’s previous agreement expired in July 2025, and they have continued working under extensions. Local 26 members authorized a strike, with an earlier potential walkout set for Nov. 1 before the deadline moved to Nov. 4 and then Friday night.
The union has accused employers of failing to make meaningful progress, while PMA has said significant differences remain after more than a year of negotiations.
The dispute is separate from the coastwide agreement covering approximately 22,000 longshore workers at 29 West Coast ports. That contract remains in effect through 2028, while Friday’s talks concern the watchmen at Los Angeles and Long Beach.

Advocates are sounding the alarm on social media as they learn from their doctors that Novartis has received reports of tumors in patients who have been treated with the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy.
Novartis’ Zolgensma has faced its share of controversy. Now, the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy is making the rounds on social media again, as patient advocates sound the alarm over tumors possibly related to the product.
“Just wanted to give people a heads-up, just got back from a neurologist appointment where we were informed that Zolgensma has been linked to two cases of kids developing tumors with seven more cases that are likely tied to it,” Dustin Brondyke, who said he has a child with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), wrote Wednesday on LinkedIn in a post shared by patient advocate Carolyn Philstrom. “Novartis, the pharmaceutical company is withholding information on some of the cases and is doing a ‘tiered rollout’ of information instead of publishing the findings,” Brondyke added.
In communications shared with BioSpace by Philstrom on Thursday morning, another parent of a child with SMA “came to know about this tumor issue last week.” The patient’s appointment was Nov. 4. “It seems Novartis has written to everyone at the same time,” the anonymous parent wrote. “So far, the two confirmed cases seems to have happened 18-60 months after dosing.”
Since Zolgensma was approved in 2019 for children under two years old with SMA, nine tumors have been reported in patients previously treated with the therapy, Novartis confirmed with BioSpace in a Thursday morning statement.
“Of those, two cases to date have shown evidence of vector integration into the DNA of the patients. In both cases, the patients underwent treatment and continue to be monitored,” the spokesperson said. “The potential risk of tumors due to vector integration is currently included in the Zolgensma prescribing information.”
Indeed, Zolgensma’s label includes a warning about the theoretical risk of tumorigenicity stemming from the gene therapy’s adeno-associated viral (AAV) vector. Seven reports of tumors have not been causally linked to the therapy.
As of Thursday, more than 6,000 patients have been treated with Zolgensma across clinical trials, managed access programs and commercial treatment, Novartis said in its email. “As part of Novartis’ ongoing commitment to monitoring the safety of our medicines, we continually evaluate new safety information and assess all reported cases.”
SMA Europe acknowledged the reports in a statement published Thursday morning.
“We understand that the relevant regulatory authorities are actively involved and are currently assessing the available evidence and determining what further steps may be needed,” the organization said. “SMA Europe has also been informed about the situation through confidential channels and have made clear to Novartis that the SMA community now needs timely public communication.”
Zolgensma uses an AAV vector to deliver a transgene encoding the human survival motor neuron (SMN) protein, which is essential for motor neuron function. SMA is caused by a mutation or deletion in the SMN1 gene.
This is not the first time Zolgensma has come under the microscope for safety concerns. The focus of previous scrutiny, however, had focused on liver-related adverse events. In September 2021, two years after Zolgensma’s approval, an FDA advisory committee was held to discuss both Novartis’ therapy and Spark Therapeutics’ Luxturna, a gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease.
About one-third of the 500 patients who had received Zolgensma at that time had experienced a liver-related adverse event, including one case of serious liver failure, according to FDA documents published at the time, Fierce Biotech reported. A summary of the adcomm meeting concluded that “Benefit-risk evaluations of AAV gene therapy (GT) products should be made on a case-by-case basis.”
The reports of tumors among patients who received Zolgensma come as Novartis is already dealing with safety concerns over its investigational CAR T therapy rapcabtagene autoleucel (rap-cel). Late this summer, it was revealed that the company had paused multiple studies of zola-cel after three patients who received the therapy died from immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome.

Ontario Energy and Mines Minister Stephen Lecce (in a file photo) says Canada still faces U.S. protectionism regardless of the midterm elections. Credit: The Northern Miner
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 5, 2026
Canada shouldn’t expect the United States to lift tariffs simply because Democrats won control of Congress , Ontario Energy and Mines Minister Stephen Lecce said.
Speaking two days after the U.S. midterm elections, Lecce said the outcome could strengthen Prime Minister Mark Carney’s negotiating position. Still, protectionism runs through both major U.S. political parties, which will leave Canadian exporters exposed even after President Donald Trump leaves office, he cautioned.
“I’m just not convinced it materially changes our fundamental reality on the ground,” Lecce said of the U.S. midterm election results in a lunchtime speech Thursday to the Empire Club of Toronto. “The change of the composition of Congress doesn’t change the policy position of America vis-a-vis tariffs.”
Lecce’s remarks underscore the gap between securing a trade agreement and eliminating tariffs. For Canadian metals producers, a trade deal may offer greater certainty without removing the tariffs that raise the cost of selling into the U.S. market.
Lame-duck Trump
Democrats won both the House of Representatives and Senate in Tuesday’s elections, giving them power to challenge Trump’s agenda when the new Congress convenes in January. The results leave the Republican president facing an opposition-controlled Congress for his final two years in office.
While U.S. political analysts pointed to voter frustration over high prices, the Iran war and government corruption as key factors behind Tuesday’s outcome, Lecce insists trade friction with Canada figured prominently in the campaign.
“Tariffs were on the ballot,” he said. “We stayed in our lane, but it’s clear that Canada was on the ballot.”
New momentum
Negotiations between the neighbours and trading partners have been showing fresh momentum. Carney said Tuesday that Washington had dropped demands affecting Canada’s ability to negotiate agreements with other countries. Trump, meanwhile, said a deal was close, Reuters reported.
Carney’s recent comments on the state of talks are “a good signal,” Lecce said. The Democrats’ win Tuesday “perhaps will enable a better hand for Prime Minister Carney and the national government to land a deal.”
Ontario Premier Doug Ford should get credit for pressing Carney to reject an earlier agreement that would have entrenched tariffs, Lecce added.
Recounting a conversation between the two leaders, Lecce said Ford told Carney this summer: “’Do not sign a bad deal that will lock us and create the precedent of acceptance of tariffs in perpetuity. No deal is materially better than a ‘good’ deal.”
Ford also made it clear to Carney that Ontario would oppose the deal publicly, according to Lecce.
Wider dispute
Ottawa suspended negotiations with the U.S. in August. Washington subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods, prompting Canadian countermeasures .
The dispute extends beyond those measures. According to Canada’s Trade Commissioner Service, U.S. sectoral tariffs on covered steel, aluminum and copper products range from 15% to 50%, subject to product and content rules. Certain other tariffs apply even when Canadian goods qualify for preferential treatment under the continental trade agreement.
The bilateral talks are unfolding alongside negotiations over the Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement, or CUSMA. The pact replaced the North American Free Trade Agreement in July 2020, following renegotiation during Trump’s first presidency.
Washington declined to extend CUSMA in its current form at the July 1 review. That triggered annual reviews rather than immediate expiry: the agreement’s existing term runs to 2036, and the three countries can jointly approve another 16-year term.
Canada has explicitly linked those discussions to relief from sectoral tariffs on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber. Preserving CUSMA and resolving the tariff dispute therefore remain connected negotiating objectives.
Diversification
Even as efforts advance to rebuild the American relationship, Canada and Ontario should continue to deepen ties with other nations, Lecce argued.
“We should strengthen that relationship [with the U.S.], get it back on track, but be very vigorous in diversification,” he said. Ontario’s goal is “to make sure we are less exposed, less shocked by that vulnerability when conservatively, well over 75% of our trade is going to one nation.”
Even so, “it doesn’t mean that we can’t hope for some return to what I’d call just normal, respectful civil dialog with the most foundational relationship on earth, which is the United States.”

2028 Porsche Panamera Facelift Spied Virtually Uncamouflaged
13 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
Porsche is not even hiding the upcoming Panamera facelift anymore, which is rather crazy when you remember that said refresh is due for 2028 in the US market. New photos reveal the regular Panamera devoid of heavy camouflage, and this regular spec indicates that Porsche has primarily focused on the bumpers.
The front end offers the clearest distinction between this base model and the previously spotted GTS , which featured a fair bit more camo. Aggressive is the word that defines the front-end styling of the GTS, with its bumper featuring prominently sculpted vertical outer intakes. The busier lower area of the bumper adds to the visual drama, but not by much over the lesser sibling.
Downgrading to the V6-powered model gets you more restrained outer intakes and cleaner lines, with the overall arrangement remaining familiar to the outgoing 2027 Panamera. Curiously enough, Porsche appears to have saved money in the lighting department. Both prototypes feature similar headlights, and everything down to the lighting signature looks unchanged from the current Panamera line.
Out back, Porsche differentiates the base and GTS through outer vents and diffuser-style elements. Despite being cleaner, the regular Panamera's rear end is way too smooth overall for a performance-oriented sedan. Understated isn't the right word here. Boring, meanwhile, fits the bill perfectly so.
Rather curiously, both the regular and the GTS come with two pairs of round exhaust outlets. By comparison, the most affordable Panamera that money can buy for 2027 comes with a single pair of trapezoidal exhaust finishers. Given the aforementioned, this regular Panamera test vehicle may be fitted with an optional exhaust system.
Photo: SH Proshots Starting at $113,000 or $1,513 per month, the 2027 Porsche Panamera for the US market is available with sport tailpipes and a sport exhaust system that includes four round outlets. What makes it a sport exhaust? As per its maker, the different mufflers help the V6 underhood exhale better.
Both prototypes retain the full-width rear light bar, with the slim element appearing identical between them. Look even closer, and you will notice a charging port on the newer prototype. This, in turn, means that we're looking at either the Panamera 4 or 4S in E-Hybrid flavor.
Both are stupidly quick, with Porsche claiming either 3.9 or 3.5 seconds to 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) if equipped with the Sport Chrono Package. Rated at 536 mechanical horsepower, the 4S E-Hybrid tops 180 miles per hour (290 kilometers) on summer performance rubber.
The 2028 model's powertrain range should hardly differ from the current one, with V8s and V8 plug-in hybrids serving as the crème de la crème. As of this writing, the GTS is the only Panamera available with V8-only muscle. Upgrading to the Turbo means plug-in assistance, yet its additional weight means little when it comes to acceleration and top speed figures.
Turbo S E-Hybrid is what Porsche calls the punchiest Panamera for 2027, whose 771 combined horsepower enables a maximum speed of 202 miles per hour (325 kilometers per hour). Zero to 60 miles per hour? Make that 2.8 seconds, thank you!

Denmark-headquartered offshore wind developer Orsted said its 704-MW Revolution Wind project off the coast of Rhode Island has reached full commercial operation. The company made the announcement in a Nov. 5 call with investors.
The project, connected to the New England grid, began producing power earlier this year. Revolution Wind is among the projects impacted by stop-work orders from the Trump administration, which has advanced policies detrimental to renewable energy and offshore wind in particular. Construction of the $6-billion installation began in 2023.
Trump administration officials in delaying offshore wind projects have said the installations could interfere with military radar. Federal judges in multiple cases have dismissed those claims and blocked the administration’s efforts to scuttle the projects.
Attorneys for the U.S. Dept. of the Interior last month asked U.S. District Court Judge Royce C. Lamberth in Washington, D.C., for permission to remand and rescind the department’s 2023 approval of the construction and operations plan for Revolution Wind. That request is still pending. Lamberth has twice previously sided with the project’s developers in lawsuits against the Trump administration.
65 Siemens Gamesa Turbines
Revolution Wind features 65 Siemens Gamesa SG 11.0-200 DD turbines, the last of which was installed in September of this year. Orsted in a statement said the installation is “generating up to its full capacity” but did not provide more details. The project has power purchase agreements with utilities in Rhode Island and Connecticut, including Eversource and United Illuminating. “This is an important milestone which provides much needed new energy generation to customers at a time when demand is rising,” Eversource spokesman William Hinkle said in a statement.
“We continue to deliver on our strategic priorities, which is translating into consistent strong financial performance,” said CEO Rasmus Errboe in discussing the company’s financial report for the first nine months of 2026. “We’ve maintained industry-leading execution across our construction pipeline, adding 1.8 GW of renewable energy capacity in Europe and the U.S. over the past few months, supporting energy security, competitiveness, and decarbonization. Our results underline our ability to deliver on our strategic priorities as planned while continuing to pursue attractive growth opportunities in our core markets. We’re well positioned to deliver a strong year for Ørsted.”
Offshore Wind Portfolio
The company in late August announced the start of commercial operation for the 913-MW Borkum Riffgrund 3 offshore wind project in the North Sea off Germany. That project is part of what the company said is part of its 8.1-GW offshore wind construction portfolio.
Orsted is continuing work on other offshore wind projects off the U.S. coast, including Sunrise Wind , a 924-MW installation off New York’s Montauk Point. It also has development plans for Skipjack Wind, a 1-GW facility off the coasts of Delaware and Maryland.
The Danish company developed the first U.S. offshore wind installation, Block Island , a 30-MW facility off Rhode Island that entered service in 2016. The company also developed the 132-MW South Fork Wind , the first offshore wind farm off the New York coast.
— Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

Chery Tiggo 2 Latin NCAP Fiasco Shows Vehicle Safety Is Only As Good as Customers Are Willing To Pay
17 photos
Photo: Latin NCAP
We've been accustomed to Chinese car models sweeping Euro NCAP tops with 5-star ratings, but safety is not the same across markets. Chery Tiggo 2 recently earned a zero-star rating from Latin NCAP, showing that some markets get the short stick of vehicle safety. To be fair, Chery has been previously flagged for poor safety and build quality in other regions, including Southeast Asia.
For those living in North America and Europe, vehicle safety is merely an afterthought. Local certification authorities are strong enough to enforce powerful standards that ensure every vehicle meets the highest safety standards. Not everyone may like that, especially when higher standards mean more electronic nannies forcing drivers to stay alert and obey traffic rules. Which, in turn, makes vehicles more expensive.
China has been showing an impressive struggle to catch up in the safety department, and the vehicles its companies sell in Europe have recently demonstrated outstanding safety. They are not only on par with European carmakers, but often setting higher standards. However, this is not true in all markets. Europeans may be spoiled with very safe Chinese vehicles, but that is not true in other markets.
Chery Tiggo 2 scored zero stars in Latin NCAP tests Chery is one of the top five Chinese carmakers, with brands such as Omoda and Jaecoo that are very popular in Europe. However, the company has also sold its products in South America under its own name. As you can expect after reading the long preamble, one of its models, the Tiggo 2, was less than impressive in Latin NCAP crash tests.
Unlike other Chery models sold in Europe, East Asia, Australia, and New Zealand, the Tiggo 2 was not only sub-par in crash safety: it was disastrous. Latin NCAP, which is South America's version of Euro NCAP, awarded the Tiggo 2 exactly zero stars, which means it's almost guaranteed to kill you in a crash. Modern vehicles usually lose crash points due to lack of advanced driver assistance features, but the Tiggo 2 is special: it also provides poor passive safety protection.
Latin NCAP, which is the New Car Assessment Program for Latin America and the Caribbean, awarded the Tiggo 2 a 0% rating for Adult Occupant Protection and 0% for Child Occupant Protection. Surprisingly, the Tiggo 2 scored better in the Pedestrian and Vulnerable Road User protection (49%), as well as Safety Assist Systems (45%), probably because it has ESC. However, it has no Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS).
Photo: Latin NCAP The Tiggo 2 comes standard with only four airbags. The model lacks head protection as standard, and rear seats are not equipped with pretensioners or load limiters. Besides that, it failed to provide structural stability during a crash, which led to high chest compression for the driver. More worryingly, a fire risk was identified during the frontal crash test.
The Tiggo 2 is an entry-level compact SUV developed specifically for emerging overseas markets such as Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East. Chery sold over 115,000 vehicles in South America in the first half of 2026 alone.
Chery is a serial offender The result has put Chery in the spotlight for poor crash safety. The Chinese carmaker has already made headlines for its Omoda 5 crossovers sold in Malaysia. Unlike the Tiggo 2, the Omoda 5 is a high-end crossover with premium features. However, that status crumbled when random Omoda 5 vehicles started losing their rear axles. The incidents, including one in early October, prompted Chery to initiate a safety recall covering almost 9,000 Omoda 4 C and H variants.
The strange part is that the same vehicles were recalled in 2024 for the same problem. At the time, the carmaker blamed an overseas component supplier for the failure. That didn't prevent the October incident, though, and the fact that Chery Chairman and President Yin Tongyue apologized does little to comfort the customers.
Photo: Latin NCAP South America has often been left behind in terms of safety, and not only by Chinese carmakers. Even European carmakers have skimped on safety in those markets, as they sought to sell their cars at rock-bottom prices. However, local customers have paid for the difference in blood, with higher casualty rates in car crashes.
Examples are more recent than car buyers in South America would like to know. Citroen Basalt, built by Stellantis in Brazil, was tested in October 2024, and it fared no better than the Tiggo 2: zero stars . Stellantis was blasted by Latin NCAP officials, who said that the carmaker does not value Latin Americans' lives as much as Indian lives. The carmaker sold the same car in India with better safety specifications, including head airbags that are missing in the South American variant.
It wasn't the only Stellantis' car model to disappoint at the time. The Citroen C3 Aircross also scored a zero-star rating in November. Renault fared no better when the Sandero was tested by Latin NCAP in December 2024. Surprisingly, the Renault Sandero scored worse than the outgoing model tested in 2019. That effectively meant that Renault, instead of improving the safety of its vehicles, made it worse.

Snowline Gold CEO Scott Berdahl at the Valley deposit in Yukon. Credit: Blair McBride
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 5, 2026
Long before Snowline Gold’s (TSX: SGD; US-OTC: SNWGF) Valley deposit attracted industry attention, cofounder and CEO Scott Berdahl struggled to find backing for the Yukon properties assembled through his family’s prospecting business.
He eventually prepared a presentation for a proposed exploration company. Investors backed the idea, and Snowline listed in March 2021.
“Snowline came out of that where I put together a slide deck really for an imaginary junior,” Berdahl told The Northern Miner in a 2023 interview . “Instead of selling the company, we ended up with investors.”
Snowline’s exploration team has won the Prospectors & Developers Association of Canada’s (PDAC) 2027 Bill Dennis Award for discovering that gold deposit, a breakthrough rooted in years of family prospecting and an early willingness to test the system’s size with bold drilling.
PDAC’s award recognizes the team’s discovery and rapid advancement of Valley, part of its Rogue project. It is among six honours recognizing achievements spanning exploration, mine financing, renewable energy, Indigenous participation and artificial intelligence. Recipients will be celebrated March 9 at Toronto’s Fairmont Royal York during PDAC’s 2027 convention.
Father-son team
Valley’s discovery drew on work begun by Ron Berdahl, Scott’s father, in 2008 and subsequent exploration by Shane and Luke Carlos. Snowline’s first four holes in 2021 all intersected gold. The following year, a 340-metre step-out returned 410 metres grading 1.89 grams gold per tonne, including 146 metres at 3.24 grams from 56 metres depth, helping establish the deposit’s scale.
By 2025, Valley hosted measured and indicated resources of 204 million tonnes grading 1.21 grams gold for 7.94 million oz., plus 44.5 million inferred tonnes at 0.62 gram gold for 890,000 ounces. A preliminary economic assessment followed that year, with a prefeasibility study expected in 2027.
“It’s the kind of deposit that you could build a major around,” Scott Berdahl told The Northern Miner in a 2025 interview.
Mexican find
Pan American Silver’s (TSX, NYSE: PAAS) La Colorada exploration team will receive the Thayer Lindsley Award for discovering the skarn deposit beneath its existing silver-lead-zinc mine in Zacatecas, Mexico.
A 2018 hole intersected about 300 metres of high-grade mineralization, validating a geological possibility considered for decades. Roughly 360,000 metres of drilling followed, outlining a large polymetallic system beneath the established operation.
Cupric Canyon Capital takes the Viola R. MacMillan Award for financing and developing Botswana’s Khoemacau copper-silver mine. The private company assembled $650 million (C$863 million at the time) in 2019 through debt, a silver stream and equity. First concentrate followed in June 2021, and MMG acquired its operating subsidiary in March 2024 in a transaction valued at about $2.1 billion, including assumed debt.
B2Gold (TSX: BTO; NYSE-A: BTG) wins the Sustainability Award for transforming the energy supply at Namibia’s Otjikoto mine. Heavy fuel oil use ended by late 2022, and renewable sources supplied about 79% of electricity by 2025 through solar generation and the national grid. The projects also trained Namibian workers and employed local contractors.
Indigenous knowledge
The Citxw Nlaka’pamux Assembly receives the Skookum Jim Award for Indigenous-led assessment and stewardship, particularly its work on the Highland Valley Copper mine extension in British Columbia.
Representing eight participating bands, the assembly developed a process incorporating Indigenous knowledge into the environmental assessment while retaining ownership and control over its collection and sharing.
Finally, SRK Consulting structural geologist Antoine Caté is the inaugural Emerging Leaders Award recipient.
PDAC recognizes his integration of geology, data science and artificial intelligence, including automated logging that identifies geological features in drillcore photographs. He also leads a multidisciplinary team connecting geoscientists and data scientists, alongside mentoring and contributing to PDAC’s technical programming.

source_document.body:
Tesla has answered NHTSA’s Special Order demanding it prove, under oath, that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. The response landed on the October 30 deadline, and Tesla asked the agency to keep all of it confidential.
The only part of the filing the public can read is a 30-page guide for firefighters. Everything about how a car with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors was certified as compliant is blacked out.
We reported in September that NHTSA had ordered Tesla to show its work on the Cybercab’s certification . The order came one week after the company started charging for Cybercab rides in Austin on September 3 and put 21 questions to the company, with civil penalties of up to $139 million for an incomplete answer and criminal exposure for a false one.
Tesla first tried to buy time. On September 18, it asked for eight more weeks, until November 20, citing “the voluminous nature of the request” and the work of searching its records and writing “thorough narrative formats in response to each question.” NHTSA gave it 30 days instead. The new deadline was October 30, and Tesla met it.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
What’s in the public docket
Three Tesla documents now sit in the AQ26002 docket, and two of them are empty.
The first is Tesla’s response letter, dated October 30 and addressed from 1 Tesla Road in Austin. It is one page long. The only text is: “The entirety of this file is confidential business information.”
The second is a placeholder for Tesla’s answer to Request 8, which asked the company to explain, standard by standard, how it determined the Cybercab complies: which subpart it certified to, and whether it ran physical tests, simulations, or engineering analyses. Per NHTSA’s note, the responsive documents carry a confidentiality request “for the entirety of each document.”
The third is the only substantive document: Tesla’s Cybercab First Responder Interaction Plan, version 1.2, dated September 3. It’s a real document with useful information in it. It’s also something Tesla has had on its website since July, aimed at police and fire crews, not regulators.
So the public gets a tow-truck manual, and the certification argument stays sealed.
The questions Tesla isn’t answering in public
The Special Order wasn’t a fishing expedition. It named the rules the Cybercab doesn’t obviously meet, and it seeks to understand how Tesla believes it can get around it.
FMVSS 135 says “the service brakes shall be activated by means of a foot control.” NHTSA has stated in public that a manufacturer of a vehicle with no foot brake can’t certify to it, then asked Tesla how it did. FMVSS 108 requires a turn-signal control that cancels itself when the steering wheel turns. FMVSS 111 requires mirrors. And the agency wanted to know whether Tesla certified the car with temporary driver controls bolted in and then removed them, which would run into the Safety Act’s “make inoperative” prohibition.
It also asked how the Cybercab is legal without a Part 555 exemption, the route Amazon’s Zoox took for its own steering-wheel-less robotaxi in July. Zoox applied, made its case, and got an exemption capped at 2,500 vehicles a year. Tesla self-certified and started charging for rides.
Every one of those answers is now under a confidentiality claim.
The firefighter guide does answer a few things
The first-responder plan was written for a different audience, but it brushes against several of NHTSA’s questions.
It says the Cybercab is “not typically equipped with a steering wheel or acceleration and brake pedals.” The word “typically” is doing work there. The same document notes that a Cybercab with a steering wheel and pedals “is typically an engineering or test vehicle, and operates at SAE Level 2 autonomy,” and includes instructions for driving one. That’s relevant to Requests 5 through 7, which asked whether the subject vehicles can be driven with temporarily attached controls.
It describes an operational design domain covering “all public roadways, such as freeways, highways, city streets, and rural roads,” at all hours, in light and moderate rain, fog, and snow. That is a far wider envelope than the Austin geofence the cars run in today, and it references an “Arizona Areas of Operation Appendix.” Request 1 asked for the ODD and Request 2 for scaling plans.
And it confirms that first responders can be granted access to on-board touchscreen controls to move the car, after showing a badge to the B-pillar camera (that’s interesting). Request 20 asked whether the touchscreen can move the vehicle and under what restrictions.
Nothing in it touches brakes, mirrors, telltales, or the certification itself.
What happens now
Confidentiality requests go to NHTSA’s Chief Counsel under Part 512. The agency decides whether Tesla’s claim holds, and it can order a public version released if it doesn’t. NHTSA hasn’t said anything about the request, and it hasn’t found the Cybercab noncompliant with any standard.
This is familiar. In June 2025, Tesla asked NHTSA to hide its answers about the original Robotaxi launch in Austin, a service running on supervised FSD while FSD was under investigation. Those answers never surfaced.
NHTSA’s opening resume for the audit put the affected population at about 1,000 vehicles. The Cybercab is still carrying passengers in Austin while the agency reads a filing nobody else can.

The VW Group's Latest MEB High-Voltage Battery Recall Now Covers 85,402 Vehicles
26 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt has recently published no fewer than four Volkswagen Group battery recalls that cover six nameplates and 85,402 vehicles worldwide. Based on the MEB platform, the nameplates in question are the Volkswagen ID.3, ID.4, ID.7, ID. Buzz, Audi Q4 e-tron, and the ID.3-derived Cupra Born.
The latest addition carries reference number 17222R and manufacturer code 93SK, with this recall involving the Q4 e-tron only. Affected compact electric sport utility vehicles were produced between November 30, 2023, and June 26, 2025. In these vehicles, the high-voltage battery is suspected to contain components that do not meet the manufacturer's specifications.
In other words, there is a risk of overheating in certain conditions. The worst-case scenario is a battery fire, which can easily consume the vehicle due to the self-sustaining chemical chain reaction inside lithium-ion batteries. More to the point, a single cell that overheats may trigger adjacent cells to fail. This reaction does not require oxygen to keep burning, making Li-Ion fires all the more dangerous.
The Audi recall may be the newest of the bunch, but the four distinct campaigns published by the Federal Motor Transport Authority of Germany do not share identical repair procedures. The original three recalls cover 72,668 vehicles from the Volkswagen and Cupra brands, with Audi's population resulting in a combined figure of 85,402 potentially affected vehicles worldwide.
93MV and 93MF are Volkswagen's recall codes, while Cupra uses 93W4. The Volkswagen campaigns reach vehicles produced between July 13, 2022, and June 27, 2025. Said programs account for 9,881 vehicles in Germany.
Photo: Volkswagen Customers are urged to recharge no higher than 80% until dealers inspect their vehicles. In the United Kingdom, the Volkswagen brand explains that some vehicles have received the charging restriction over the air. Cupra used the same approach for the Born, with Cupra further claiming that keeping the battery just below its full state of charge reduces the load on the high-voltage system.
Not going over 80% also provides a safety margin while techs carry out inspections. Regarding the remedy, Volkswagen and Cupra owners will first receive letters containing hi-vis warning stickers. Yeah, thanks a bunch! The warning stickers are intended to prevent drivers from overlooking the 80% limit.
The next stage requires updated software designed to monitor the battery module for possible abnormalities. Said code also displays relevant warnings at an early stage, minimizing the risk of a thermal event. If the inspection or subsequent battery monitoring identifies a battery-related issue, dealers may replace individual modules or the entire high-voltage battery.
Cupra acknowledges individual cases with property damage, but thankfully, there are no confirmed reports of personal injury. Even if the battery's SoC is restricted to 80%, all brands allow customers to recharge on direct current. Battery checks in the workshop shouldn't take more than an hour.
Audi's procedure, meanwhile, begins with a battery data inspection at authorized service centers. The result determines if the charging restriction to 80% is removed or kept in place until the final corrective measure becomes available. Although KBA information describes module or battery pack replacements, Audi says the final repair is currently under development.
In the United States market, no fewer than 9,048 examples of the Q4 e-tron are being recalled. Audi uses the same 93SK code for them, and known customers are to be notified through interim letters via first-class mail no later than December 18, 2026.

Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash.
Hyundai recalls Kona Electric and Veloster N models
In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.
The recall impacts 37,901 vehicles in total, including 29,058 Kona Electric and 8,843 Veloster N models.
According to documents submitted to the NHTSA, the issue stems from a software error with the airbag control unit (ACU) that can cause the airbag malfunction indicator light (MIL) to come on and the airbag system to deactivate under certain driving conditions.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The data may become corrupted during a system reboot or power interruption while the system is writing to the ACU’s memory. When this happens, the airbag MIL will illuminate to warn drivers.
As of October 22, 2026, Hyundai is aware of 331 alleged incidents related to the issue. However, none have resulted in a crash, fire, or injury.
2023 Hyundai Kona Electric (Source: Hyundai)
Owners can take their vehicle to the closest dealer, where it will update the ACU software, free of charge.
Hyundai expects to mail out owner notification letters on January 1, 2027. In the meantime, owners can contact Hyundai’s customer service at 1-855-371-9460 with any questions or concerns. Hyundai’s recall number is 311.
You can also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit the NHTSA.gov website for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V728.

2028 BMW iX2 LCI Shows New Face With Neue Klasse Stylistic Influences
16 photos
Photo: Baldauf
Without changing too much of the underpinnings, the iX2 prepares for a 2028 model year facelift with a Neue Klasse flavor. Clad in camo, this prototype of the zero-emission crossover dons a new interpretation of the iX3's grille, slimmer headlights, and slightly different rear signature lighting.
Sharing the Untere Klasse platform with the X2, the fully electric brother looks a lot better with the Neue Klasse-inspired front end. Narrow LED units are neatly positioned toward the outer edges of the fascia, making the iX2 appear wider and more elegant at the same time without compromising its sporty aesthetic.
The narrower, more upright proportions introduced by the Neue Klasse models are complemented by a dark connecting element between the headlights, and the lower part of the bumper also features revised detailing. For cooling purposes, two large openings with active shutters can be seen right below the grille area.
Very familiar from the sides, the iX2 retains the current iteration's rising window line, sloping roofline, and large rear quarter windows. Pull-up door handles are on the menu as well, as is a clean-looking rear bumper and a similarly clean valance panel. Out there, the rear lights appear to be the only noticeable update.
Just like the internal combustion 3 Series, which is extremely similar to the i3 both inside and out despite having completely different underpinnings, the iX2 should adopt iDrive X with Panoramic Vision. This change may also bring forth a larger-than-life central touchscreen with a 17.9-inch diagonal. Panoramic Vision, meanwhile, replaces the now-familiar digital instrument cluster.
Photo: Baldauf Projected information across the lower portion of the windshield is the name of the game, and given time, all BMWs are expected to adopt this system. Although certain models based on the Cluster Architecture received Gen6 eDrive goodies from Neue Klasse models, the iX2 is rumored to retain Gen5 eDrive tech.
BMW has already updated the powertrain this year, introducing new silicon-carbide semiconductor components in the power electronics for improved efficiency. Shared with the iX1, the SiC inverter enables a driving range of up to 514 kilometers (320 miles) for the eDrive20 version of the iX1.
The xDrive30, meanwhile, tops 466 kilometers (290 miles) in the WLTP. Solid numbers for small crossovers, and good enough not to warrant a major powertrain update. As ever, BMW is believed to sell front- and all-wheel-drive versions of the iX2. The current versions are referred to as eDrive20 and xDrive30, with prices kicking off at 51,000 euros in the German automaker's home market.
Production should kick off in July 2027, making it a 2028 model by US standard, but you won't find the revised iX2 at US dealers. Why is that? You can blame America's preferences for larger electric sport utility vehicles, and truth be told, BMW prefers to sell you the iX3 and iX4 because those babies yield higher margins.
BMW's Regensburg plant has recently produced its nine millionth vehicle, and iX2 production will continue there. Said facility also serves as the home of the internal combustion X2, which is available with either 1.5- or 2.0-liter mills. The punchiest of the lost is the M35i with xDrive, whose 2.0-liter unit develops a very respectable 300 ps in Europe or 312 hp in the United States market.

BYD launched the new Seal 07 in China, where it starts at around $23,000. It’s about the size of a Toyota Camry, but brings a surprising amount of tech and premium features for the money.
BYD launches second-gen Seal 07 with Flash Charging
After introducing the updated first-generation Seal 07 in March, BYD launched the second-gen model on Thursday.
The second-generation Seal 07, which BYD calls the “new choice for a class-leading luxury experience,” is available in battery electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains.
BYD offers five variants, including two PHEVs and three EVs, starting at 139,900 yuan (about $21,000) for the plug-in hybrid and 149,900 yuan (around $22,500) for the fully electric version.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new Seal 07 EV uses a 76.7 kWh second-generation BYD Blade LFP battery, providing a CLTC range of up to 481 miles (775 km).
It comes standard with a single rear-mounted electric motor producing up to 328 hp (245 kW) and 269 lb-ft (365 Nm) of torque, which BYD says enables it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 5.5 seconds.
All plug-in hybrid variants use BYD’s latest DM-i system, which features a 1.5L turbocharged engine with 154 hp (115 kW) and a 214 hp (160 kW) front electric motor.
The new Seal 07 PHEV has a smaller 37 kWh battery that provides up to 205 miles (330 km) of pure electric CLTC range. That’s a considerable jump from the 143 miles (230 km) of electric range the previous generation offered.
Thanks to BYD’s latest Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. To go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.
Both versions are 5,080 mm long, 1,960 mm wide, and 1,495 mm tall, with a 2,960 mm wheelbase, which is slightly bigger than the Toyota Camry.
Inside, the new Seal 07 adopts BYD’s latest cabin design, including a 15.6″ floating center infotainment screen, a 10.25″ instrument cluster, and two rear passenger entertainment screens.
BYD added several premium extras, including a built-in 6.8L smart refrigerator, zero gravity seats, and driver headrest audio. It also offers the most rear passenger space and the largest frunk (160L) in its class, according to BYD.
The Seal 07 debuts BYD’s Smart Ecosystem 2.0, including “Diva,” a smartwatch that can interact with the vehicle and let drivers manage functions remotely.
Higher-priced models offer BYD’s God’s Eye B intelligent driving system, with a roof-mounted LiDAR available as an option. The setup provides safety and convenience features such as Navigation on Autopilot in the city and on highways, plus full-scenario intelligent parking.
BYD is offering a limited-time “Super trade-in price” promo, starting at 145,900 yuan ($22,000) for the new Seal 07 EV and 135,900 yuan ($20,500) for the PHEV version.
